source_evidence.anchor: Proposition 2.7.1 heading and opening equivalence sentence
source_evidence.observation: For a random variable X, the proposition declares properties (a)--(d) equivalent and says that their positive parameters differ by at most an absolute constant factor.

source_evidence.anchor: Footnote 7 attached to the absolute-constant-factor assertion
source_evidence.observation: The printed precise meaning is that there is an absolute constant C such that property i with parameter K_i implies property j with a parameter K_j satisfying K_j <= C K_i, for i,j = 1,2,3,4.
Property (a) is the tail estimate P{|X| >= t} <= 2 exp(-t/K_1) for every t >= 0; property (b) is the moment estimate ||X||_{L_p} = (E|X|^p)^(1/p) <= K_2 p for every p >= 1.
Property (c) is E exp(lambda |X|) <= exp(K_3 lambda) for every lambda with 0 <= lambda <= 1/K_3; property (d) is E exp(|X|/K_4) <= 2.
If E X = 0, the proposition additionally declares (a)--(d) equivalent to (e): E exp(lambda X) <= exp(K_5^2 lambda^2) for every lambda with |lambda| <= 1/K_5.

binders: Positive parameters K_1, K_2, K_3, and K_4 for properties (a), (b), (c), and (d), respectively.
Under the additional assumption E X = 0, a positive parameter K_5 for property (e).
hypotheses: No centering assumption is imposed for the equivalence of properties (a)--(d).
The additional equivalence with property (e) assumes E X = 0.
conclusions: Properties (a)--(d) are equivalent, with their admissible positive parameters comparable up to an absolute constant factor.
(a) For all t >= 0, P{|X| >= t} <= 2 exp(-t/K_1).
(c) For all lambda satisfying 0 <= lambda <= 1/K_3, E exp(lambda |X|) <= exp(K_3 lambda).
If E X = 0, properties (a)--(d) are also equivalent to (e): for all lambda satisfying |lambda| <= 1/K_5, E exp(lambda X) <= exp(K_5^2 lambda^2).
definitions_and_conventions: The MGF expressions in (c), (d), and (e) are expectations of exponential functions; (c) and (d) use |X|, whereas (e) uses X itself.

The source's explicit parameter-comparison convention for (a)--(d) is: there exists an absolute constant C such that property i with K_i implies property j with some K_j <= C K_i for any i,j in {1,2,3,4}.
implicit_context: Probability and expectation are taken with respect to the probability law of X.
An absolute constant is independent of X and of the particular admissible parameter value.
Each property is an existence-of-a-positive-parameter condition, and equivalence includes quantitative conversion of admissible parameters rather than merely qualitative finiteness.

details: The result is an equivalence among parameterized properties, with universal constant-factor control on parameter conversion.
The equivalence must preserve each property's full quantified range and numerical form.
The tail decay is exponential in t/K_1 and carries the leading factor 2.
The L_p moments grow at most linearly in p for every p >= 1.
Property (c) controls E exp(lambda |X|) throughout the closed one-sided interval 0 <= lambda <= 1/K_3.
Property (d) is a single-point exponential-moment bound with threshold 2.
Only when E X = 0, property (e) controls the signed MGF on the closed two-sided interval |lambda| <= 1/K_5.
The exponent in (e) is quadratic, K_5^2 lambda^2, despite the underlying exponential-tail class.

undebatable_constraints: X is not assumed centered for properties (a)--(d); E X = 0 is specifically required for the additional equivalence with (e).
All parameters K_1 through K_5 that occur are positive.
Property (a) quantifies over every t >= 0 and has exactly the bound 2 exp(-t/K_1).
Property (b) quantifies over every p >= 1 and has linear growth K_2 p for (E|X|^p)^(1/p).
Property (c) uses |X| and only nonnegative lambda in the closed interval [0,1/K_3], with right side exp(K_3 lambda).
Property (d) is the single bound E exp(|X|/K_4) <= 2.
Property (e) uses X rather than |X|, quantifies over the closed two-sided interval |lambda| <= 1/K_5, and has right side exp(K_5^2 lambda^2).
The equivalence is quantitative: admissible parameters are related up to an absolute multiplicative constant, not merely asserted to exist without comparison.
The one-sided absolute-value MGF condition (c) and the two-sided centered signed-MGF condition (e) are distinct and must not be conflated.

ambiguities.issue: The footnote's formal parameter-comparison statement explicitly indexes only properties 1--4, while the subsequent moreover-clause adds property (e) under centering.
ambiguities.evidence: Footnote 7 on PDF page 20 (printed page 31) states the C-factor implication for i,j = 1,2,3,4; PDF pages 21--22 (printed pages 32--33) then prove (b) <=> (e) with absolute numerical constants after normalization.
ambiguities.impact: The source unambiguously asserts qualitative equivalence of (e) with (a)--(d) when E X = 0, and its proof supplies constant-factor conversions between (b) and (e), but the footnote's literal indexed formulation does not itself mention K_5.

contracts.contract_plain_english: A random variable has exponential tails exactly when its L_p moments grow at most linearly in p, equivalently when its absolute-value exponential moments satisfy either the stated local-in-lambda bound or the stated single-point bound; the admissible scale parameters convert into one another within universal constant factors. If the variable is centered, these are also equivalent to a quadratic bound on the signed MGF for lambda in a neighborhood of zero.
